statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is 40, moderate, as the 50% US tariff on Canadian goods and Ottawa's pledged dollar-for-dollar match sit alongside a Tesla recall of roughly three million vehicles and an already tight energy backdrop, none of which any venue can price before Sunday.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open and left VIX at 14.89 near the session low, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, thirteen hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a tradable price path rather than a view on direction. Stress stays in the moderate band and drifts modestly higher across the weekend as reciprocal North American tariffs, a large single-name recall, Russian refining outages and a closed Strait of Hormuz accumulate with no venue able to price them. No danger window is published because no trading session falls inside the horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours while reciprocal 50% US-Canada tariffs and a three-million-vehicle Tesla recall accumulate as unpriced weekend risk, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T10:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T09:00:00Z and end thirteen hours before the reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. One quote source read materially away from that print during this run while a second matched it exactly, so the level is published from the corroborated reading and Confidence is trimmed a point rather than raised. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00% and near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. The most recent Federal Reserve H.15 daily column, for 20 August, shows the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23% after the bond selloff earlier in the week, with the 30-year reported at its highest since 2007. WTI is $87.06 and Brent $94.39, both roughly 37-39% higher than a year ago with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed since late February and the US-Iran ceasefire lapsed with talks described as static. Three developments were verified after the close. US-Canada trade negotiations were suspended on Friday night and a 50% US tariff on about $28 billion of Canadian goods took effect at midnight, with Ottawa pledging to match it dollar for dollar. Tesla announced a recall of roughly 2.98 million vehicles over retractable door handles that may be hard to operate after a severe collision, the largest automotive recall in China's history, landing after TSLA closed 5.14% higher on Friday. Reporting ahead of the coming week frames the Nvidia print and the Jackson Hole symposium as the tests of this year's rally, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index down about 5% over the week. All three add to the unpriced weekend stack rather than to any observable price path. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is directionally benign but internally mixed: index futures firm with NQ +0.30% and ES +0.38%, VIX futures -1.68%, gold +2.39%, Treasury futures slightly lower, megacaps split five to three positive with 1.82 points of dispersion, and semiconductors net negative on ARM -2.95% and INTC -2.24% against AVGO +1.21%. That conflict lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail, and it is delayed context in any case. Because no price path can develop in any published hour, Tail holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Stress opens at 40 and drifts to 44 by the final slot, remaining inside the moderate band. Confidence opens at 87 and eases to 81 as the last live observation ages past thirty-four hours. The week beyond the horizon is dense: core PCE, the second Q2 GDP estimate and durable goods on Wednesday at 12:30Z, Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 results after that day's close, and the Jackson Hole symposium from Thursday with the Fed chair's keynote at 14:00Z on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 21 hourly assessments are available and 3 clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable, one at the start of the window on 21 August and two in the 22 August pre-dawn window. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent with the session that produced it: 13 through the European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, a step down to 10 at 20:00Z and then to 5 and 4 once the 21:00Z halt removed price discovery. Stress fell in parallel from a 58 peak at the open to 35-39 overnight as realised volatility decayed and VIX closed near its session low, then edged back to 39 as the tariff and refinery headlines landed. Confidence stayed in the 84-88 high band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T09:00:00Z and ends thirteen hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress opens at 40, eases to 38 through the quiet Saturday afternoon window when weekend news flow is thinnest, then drifts to 44 by the final slot as reciprocal North American tariffs, a three-million-vehicle Tesla recall, Russian refining outages and a six-month Hormuz closure accumulate without a venue able to price them; it stays inside the moderate band throughout. Confidence opens at 87 on a well-verified but settled evidence set and eases to 81 as the newest live observation passes thirty-four hours old. Dominant mode is normal in every slot, which records the absence of tradable structure rather than a directional view. No danger window is published because no trading session falls inside the horizon; the first genuine checkpoints are the Sunday 22:00Z reopen and then Wednesday's 12:30Z core PCE, GDP and durable goods block.
